subject: Definite sampler coordinate mismatch: translator always expects normalized native sampler
body: Additional exact sampler contract evidence, stronger than filter-only concerns: pinned vk/structs.rs203..205 explicitly states unnormalizedCoordinates is NEVER set; Metal pixel-coordinate samplers are handled in the shader. ash_interop/convert.rs151 sets .unnormalized_coordinates(false). lower/sampler/shared.rs419..442 normalizes pixel coordinates in shader by dividing by base texture size. Current bridge fills native s.normalized from original D2_NORMALIZED, which runtime copies from the original Metal descriptor. Thus a Metal pixel sampler (normalizedCoordinates=false) reaches an unnormalized hardware sampler even though the translated shader already normalizes it. This is a direct coordinate-semantics mismatch for runtime samplers that use the sampling path. Include linear pixel-coordinate sampler in the real producer/wire regression, with native normalized=1 for translated programs. Nearest pixel shaders may choose pure fetch and not consume a sampler, so use a shader/path that actually samples. Original Metal coordinate flag must remain in translator specialization/input facts; the resolved native sampler must be separate. Sources are pinned local translator; no runtime/hardware inference required and no edit/build by audit.
